primary_source.citation: Riihimäki M, Hemminki A, Sundquist J, Hemminki K. Patterns of metastasis in colon and rectal cancer. Scientific Reports. 2016;6:29765.
primary_source.study_type: Population-based registry study; Swedish Cancer Registry linked with National Patient Register and Cause of Death Register; n=17,811 rectal cancer patients

biomarkers.name: KRAS, NRAS, BRAF V600E, HER2, MSI/dMMR, NTRK/ALK/ROS1/RET fusions
biomarkers.prevalence: Broadly similar molecular testing paradigm to left-sided colon cancer; RAS mutations are common, BRAF V600E and MSI/dMMR are less frequent in rectum than in right colon; HER2 amplification and kinase fusions are uncommon but actionable in selected cases
biomarkers.clinical_use: Same targeted-therapy landscape as COLON_ADENOCARCINOMA — rectal is biologically part of the CRC continuum

biomarkers.name: MSI / dMMR
biomarkers.prevalence: ~5-10% of rectal adenocarcinomas (lower than right colon)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Neoadjuvant dostarlimab monotherapy — Cercek et al. NEJM 2022 reported 100% complete clinical response in the initial dMMR locally advanced rectal cancer cohort (n=12); subsequent expansion maintained very high response rates, supporting organ-preserving nonoperative management in selected patients

biomarkers.name: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Investigational/adjunctive for post-TNT response prediction and MRD monitoring; not yet standard-alone for watch-and-wait candidate selection

biomarkers.name: MRI tumour regression grade (mrTRG)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Assesses response to neoadjuvant CRT / TNT; contributes to watch-and-wait vs surgery decision

biomarkers.name: CEA, CA 19-9
biomarkers.clinical_use: CEA is standard for surveillance monitoring; CA 19-9 is not a routine standard surveillance biomarker for rectal adenocarcinoma

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Adenocarcinoma similar to colon; distal location; anatomic constraint drives distinct treatment approach
variants: medullary (rare; typically MSI-H/dMMR, uncommon in rectum)

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Similar spectrum to colon — MSI-H/dMMR is uncommon in rectum (~5-10% and lower than right colon)

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Intestinal stem/progenitor cells at the crypt base of rectal mucosa
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Same intestinal-type glandular differentiation as colon adenocarcinoma; CMS2 (canonical) and CMS4 (mesenchymal) are common CRC transcriptional programs, but no single CMS predominance is specific enough for routine rectal classification
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Same adenoma-carcinoma sequence as left-sided colon is common (e.g., APC → KRAS/NRAS → TP53), with additional actionable alterations in a minority such as ERBB2 amplification and rare NTRK/ALK/ROS1/RET fusions
